title: Wearable activity feedback after total knee replacement: a rapid review to inform a device lease decision
abstract: Objective: to update the evidence on whether wearable-based activity feedback after primary total knee replacement improves patient-reported function at about three months, and to summarise adherence, physiotherapist time and results for older and digitally excluded patients. Design: rapid review with a dated update search from January 2022, single screening with a 20 percent check and stated shortcuts. Results and conclusions will be written after the synthesis.
introduction: Activity trackers with feedback raise step counts after knee replacement, but whether they improve function is uncertain and the most recent synthesis searched to March 2022. A regional centre must decide whether to lease devices for about 900 patients a year, a third of them aged 75 or over.
methods: Three bibliographic databases and two trial registries were searched from January 2022 to October 2026 and the 2023 meta-analysis was used as the base. Randomised trials informed effectiveness; qualitative and observational studies informed adherence, workload and experience. Function at about three months was pooled with a random-effects model when at least five trials reported it.
results: No studies have been screened yet. The report will present the search flow, the updated pooled estimate for function with its certainty, step counts, adherence at 6 and 12 weeks, physiotherapist time and results for older patients where reported.
discussion: The discussion will weigh a probable step count gain against the size and certainty of any function gain, set adherence and workload against the lease cost, and state what a local evaluation would need to measure if the committee proceeds.
limitations: Shortcuts may miss studies; English only; no author contact; few trials report results for patients over 75.
conclusion: To be written after the synthesis; it will be limited to what the evidence shows about function, adherence and workload and will not claim benefits for groups the trials did not include.
reportingChecklist: PRISMA 2020, with the rapid review shortcuts listed
summary: PRISMA-structured draft with results left empty until the synthesis.
